method.label: Construct roots and prove the set stops

annotationRationale: Integer-root divisibility restricts every new nonzero element to a signed divisor of 10. Proving this restriction is preserved, then constructing every candidate, establishes the complete final set.
sourceMethod: Follows the official successive polynomial constructions and Rational Root Theorem bound. It handles zero constant terms by first factoring out powers of the variable and explains the integer-root divisibility argument directly.

review.mathCheck: All seven constructions use available coefficients and have the stated roots. For a nonzero polynomial, removing its lowest power of the variable gives a nonzero constant coefficient c; any nonzero integer root r satisfies r|c|10. Thus the constructed set is closed and contains exactly 9 elements, choice D. Zero roots and zero constant terms are handled.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of MAA solution 21 on page 9: construct the signed divisors, then apply integer-root divisibility. The candidate supplies a valid elementary proof and explicitly handles the zero-constant-term case.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed integer-solution and invariant nodes fit both the restriction and reachability arguments. Factors and multiples is appropriate background; no material concept is missing.
